$comment: Rivals, election night, returning visitors, away, monuments, Grand Projects, twists and pair names, captions, places. Assembled by content-assemble from lines-rivals, lines-returning, lines-shelf, governor-places-runup.

rivals.name: Councillor Prudence Stitchley
rivals.backAgain: Councillor Stitchley is back for another go. Same hat. She has had it brushed.
rivals.resignation: Councillor Stitchley won, then resigned to spend more time with her hat.
rivals.note: slogan, resignation and night line given (spec 2.10, 4.4, style sheet 2)

rivals.name: Cyril Dunnock
rivals.backAgain: Cyril Dunnock is back for another go. He is waiting politely on the step.
rivals.resignation: Cyril Dunnock won, then resigned to spend more time with his doorbells. He has gone to answer one.
rivals.note: hobby 'doorbells' as the style sheet has it; names.json role still says 'door knockers' (requested)

rivals.name: Philippa Setter
rivals.backAgain: Philippa Setter is back for another go. Her leaflet is a crossword. Nobody has finished it.
rivals.resignation: Philippa Setter won, then resigned to spend more time with her crosswords. Her notice was eleven across.

rivals.name: Leander Waft
rivals.backAgain: Leander Waft is back for another go. He has had the spoon engraved: AGAIN.
rivals.resignation: Leander Waft won, then resigned to spend more time with the Ceremonial Spoon. It is his turn to hold it.
rivals.note: slogan given; role line on papers is names.json's "Keeper, Ceremonial Spoon"

rivals.name: Hortensia Mallowby
rivals.backAgain: Hortensia Mallowby is back for another go. The accordion is wearing a rosette.
rivals.resignation: Hortensia Mallowby won, then resigned to spend more time with her accordion. It was waiting, half open.
rivals.note: the slogan is how an accordion is played, and how the desk is

rivals.name: Fergus Noonday
rivals.backAgain: Fergus Noonday is back for another go. He arrived at noon exactly, by his own reckoning.
rivals.resignation: Fergus Noonday won, then resigned to spend more time with his sundials. The afternoons, mostly.
rivals.note: weather no worse than cloud (style sheet 1)

rivals.name: Professor Ozias Kalends
rivals.backAgain: Professor Kalends is back for another go. He has started on Thursdays.
rivals.resignation: Professor Kalends won, then resigned to spend more time with his calendars. Effective last Wednesday.

rivals.name: Ottoline Strop
rivals.backAgain: Ottoline Strop is back for another go. She has brought her own chair, and a cushion for it.
rivals.resignation: Ottoline Strop won, then resigned to spend more time with her chairs. She has not yet chosen one.
rivals.note: slogan given; role line on papers is names.json's "Folded Napkin (Second Class)"

rivals.name: Lettice Ringrose
rivals.backAgain: Lettice Ringrose is back for another go. She rang ahead to say so.
rivals.resignation: Lettice Ringrose won, then resigned to spend more time with her handbells. All twelve were consulted.

rivals.name: Aldous Mould
rivals.backAgain: Aldous Mould is back for another go. He says the heap has been building up to this.
rivals.resignation: Aldous Mould won, then resigned to spend more time with his compost heap. It had been expecting him.

rivals.name: Araminta Dovecote
rivals.backAgain: Araminta Dovecote is back for another go. A pigeon brought the news ahead of her.
rivals.resignation: Araminta Dovecote won, then resigned to spend more time with her pigeons. They had written to her.
rivals.note: homing pigeons; the pigeons are only kept and admired

rivals.name: Ivo Pharos
rivals.backAgain: Ivo Pharos is back for another go. He has brought a model lighthouse. It is switched on.
rivals.resignation: Ivo Pharos won, then resigned to spend more time with his model lighthouses. One needed a new bulb.

rivals.name: Honoria Lathe
rivals.backAgain: Honoria Lathe is back for another go. She has left a space in the tapestry for it.
rivals.resignation: Honoria Lathe won, then resigned to spend more time with her tapestry. It shows her winning, then resigning.

rivals.name: Quentin Furlong
rivals.backAgain: Quentin Furlong is back for another go. He played himself in. It took a while.
rivals.resignation: Quentin Furlong won, then resigned to spend more time with his harmonica. He played his notice.
rivals.note: a harmonica sounds on the breath in and out

rivals.name: Imogen Tessel
rivals.backAgain: Imogen Tessel is back for another go. She has done the edges.
rivals.resignation: Imogen Tessel won, then resigned to spend more time with her jigsaws of sky. It is going well, she thinks.

rivals.name: Rufus Pantry
rivals.backAgain: Rufus Pantry is back for another go. He tapped the glass before coming. It said 'fair'.
rivals.resignation: Rufus Pantry won, then resigned to spend more time with his barometers. All of them saw it coming.

rivals.name: Gertrude Ambling
rivals.backAgain: Gertrude Ambling is back for another go. She walked here. It took a week, by choice.
rivals.resignation: Gertrude Ambling won, then resigned to spend more time with her walking boots. They were waiting by the door.

rivals.name: Bartholomew Knapp
rivals.backAgain: Bartholomew Knapp is back for another go. You may have heard him arrive.
rivals.resignation: Bartholomew Knapp won, then resigned to spend more time with his yodelling. He announced it from a hill.

night.text: Stitchley: I still own the hat.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: stitchley

night.text: Dunnock: Nobody is home, then. Understood.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: dunnock

night.text: Setter: Defeated. Eight letters. I checked.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: setter

night.text: Waft: The spoon will be disappointed. I shall tell it gently.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: waft

night.text: Mallowby: I shall play something short on the way out. In a minor key.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: mallowby

night.text: Noonday: It was never my hour. It has clouded over anyway.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: noonday

night.text: Kalends: I have crossed out today. It will not be missed.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: kalends

night.text: Strop: I shall remain seated. Thank you.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: strop

night.text: Ringrose: The handbells would like to congratulate you. One at a time.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: ringrose

night.text: Mould: Nothing is wasted. I shall put this evening on the heap.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: mould

night.text: Dovecote: I shall send word. By the usual route.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: dovecote

night.text: Pharos: I shall leave a small light on for you.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: pharos

night.text: Lathe: I shall add this evening to the tapestry. A small corner.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: lathe

night.text: Furlong: A short tune for the winner. Very short.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: furlong

night.text: Tessel: There is always one piece missing. I will look under the table.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: tessel

night.text: Pantry: Unsettled, then. I shall take my coat.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: pantry

night.text: Ambling: I shall walk home. The scenic way.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: ambling

night.text: Knapp: I shall congratulate you properly. Please stand well back.
night.note: the rival's line at the result: knapp

night.text: Good evening. I will read each envelope once. Applause after, please.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Good evening. I have a new stick of chalk, and a spare.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Held. One rosette, pinned straight.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Held. For the back of the room: held.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Not held. I will chalk it neatly, all the same.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: To your opponent. The rosette goes back in its box.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: That is a majority. The band may begin.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: That is a majority. Please do not cut anything yet.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: That is a majority for your opponent. I will read the rest, as is proper.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Your opponent has a majority. The band will play something quieter.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: Quiet at the back, please. Thank you.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

night.text: A reminder: the tea urn is off during the reading.
night.note: Agatha Tallow, straight and procedural

returning.text: The same paper as before. It has been ironed.
The same paper. The visitor hopes you have changed instead.
Back again. Cuthbert has filed it under AGAIN.
This paper has been here before. This time it wiped its feet.
Back again. Rodney advises you to look as if you remember it.
The same request, now with a covering letter about the request.
Back again. They say it is a different paper. It is the same paper.
Word for word as before. They practised on the stairs.
Back again. Gwendolyn has the old answer ready, if you want to save time.
Here once more, with the same words, said more slowly.
A fresh envelope. The words inside are not fresh.
Back again. They have brought their own chair.
Back again. They now know everyone in the corridor by name.
The request is the same. The handwriting is neater.
Returned, unchanged, with a note pinned on: STILL ASKING.
Back again, by appointment. They made the appointment.
They have heard you like ribbons. There is one round it now.
Back again. It says it was in the area.
Back again, at exactly the same time as last time.
Back again. You have been spotted, and it is in the notebook.
Back again, with the same paper and a fresh flask. They expect a wait.
Back again. Your office is now a request stop in their notebook.
Back again. There is a footnote now, and it has a footnote.
Back again, with the timetable of their next visit attached.
Back again. The paper has spent the week in a shop window.
Back again. They have looked at your office window and have notes.
Back again. The paper has been dressed for the season.
Back again, in a frame, lit from below.
Back again. They rang the bell at your door. Your door has no bell.
Returned in tissue paper, with a bow tied at a careful angle.
Back again, with the same pumpkin and a firmer tone.
The paper has been entered for a rosette. It was highly commended.
Back again. It has been turned once a day, so it ripens evenly.
Back again. They have weighed the paper, for fairness.
Back again. They brought the paper in a wheelbarrow, out of habit.
Back again. It has been kept in a cool, dry place, as the label says.
Back again, humming the request under their breath.
The request has since been arranged for full band.
The same request, now with a second verse.
Back again. The paper now has its own music stand.
A cornet waits in the corridor, in case your answer needs a fanfare.
The paper is back, written a little louder.
Back again, so quietly you almost missed it.
The paper came back under the door without a sound.
Back again. They have sat in the corridor since dawn, perfectly still.
Back again. They have not said a word. They are waiting for a bite.
They waited by the water cooler, as if it were a pond.
Back again. They ask that you sign or study it quietly.
Back again. They looked up at your ceiling first, out of habit.
The paper has a tail on it now, for steadiness.
Back again. They have opened your window, just in case.
The paper arrived slightly before they did.
Back again, folded into something that very nearly flies.
Back again. They have let out a little more string.
Back again. They have seen your office plant and are not mentioning it.
Back again. The margins have been measured, twice.
Your pens are now in a straight line. They did that while waiting.
Back again, with shears, in case the paper needs editing.
The paper has been clipped since. Only the parts that stuck out.
Back again. They have checked that your desk is level. It is not.

away.text: The clock chimed the hours without you. It managed.
Cuthbert put the stationery cupboard in order, then the stationery.
Gwendolyn balanced the books, then, to pass the time, balanced them again.
Rodney told the newspaper you were working very hard elsewhere.
Your desk wore a sign saying BACK SHORTLY. It has been very patient.
The ministries collected without you. Gwendolyn says they barely noticed.
Rodney wrote a speech for your return. It is mostly about you.
A committee watered the office plant, after a short meeting.
Your photograph kept an eye on things. It has nothing to report.
Your chair was kept warm by a cushion with your name on it.

monuments.name: A bust of yourself
monuments.text: In bronze, facing the door, so that visitors meet you twice.

monuments.name: A bust of the bust
monuments.text: The first bust looked lonely. This one gazes at it, admiringly.

monuments.name: Bronze ribbon scissors
monuments.text: They can no longer cut anything. You still bring them to openings.

monuments.name: A ribbon, cut, in bronze
monuments.text: Cut by you, then cast in bronze. It cannot be cut again, which you regret.

monuments.name: Your parking space, in bronze
monuments.text: Nobody may park on it now. You park beside it and visit.

monuments.name: A hat with a smaller hat on it
monuments.text: Cast from Tobias Slake's gift. He has since sent a smaller hat, for the top.

monuments.name: The prize pumpkin, in bronze
monuments.text: Cast from the prize pumpkin itself, which sat very still for it.

monuments.name: A bench with your name
monuments.text: Your name runs along the backrest in raised letters. Visitors leave wearing it.

monuments.name: A plaque to the plaque
monuments.text: It marks the unveiling of the first plaque. A third will mark this one.

monuments.name: Your first pen
monuments.text: The pen that signed your first paper. You had not read that one either.

monuments.name: The in-tray, empty at last
monuments.text: Cast on the one afternoon it was empty. There is a photograph.

monuments.name: A committee of three chairs
monuments.text: Three bronze chairs face each other. They have not yet decided.

monuments.name: A fountain shaped like you
monuments.text: Lavinia Plash calls it a perfect likeness. It, too, never stops talking.

monuments.name: Your umbrella, in bronze
monuments.text: Crispin Mizzle's gift, cast so that it can never be lost. Nor opened.

monuments.name: A pothole, preserved
monuments.text: The oldest pothole there is, behind a rope. You opened it to the public.

monuments.name: A handshake with yourself
monuments.text: Both hands are yours. Both look delighted to meet you.

monuments.name: The most adequate trophy
monuments.text: Awarded to you, by you, for adequacy. The engraving is adequate.

monuments.name: A sundial set by you
monuments.text: It tells the time by your arrival, so you have never once been late.

monuments.name: A bandstand for one
monuments.text: There is room for you and a music stand. The band sends its regards.

monuments.name: A kite that will not fly
monuments.text: Bronze, string and all. It was flown once, by crane, for the photograph.

monuments.name: A teapot that chimes
monuments.text: A gift from Till's Teas. It chimes on the hour and pours on the half.

monuments.name: A duck, unveiled
monuments.text: The duck you once fed, on camera. It came to the unveiling, briefly.

monuments.name: A rosette of rosettes
monuments.text: Every rosette you ever pinned on yourself, sewn into one. All first prize.

monuments.name: You, pointing at something
monuments.text: A statue of you, pointing boldly to the future. The future is the bus station.

grandProjects.name: The Very Long Bridge
grandProjects.text: It crosses the river, then carries on, in case the river moves.

grandProjects.name: The National Ribbon Mill
grandProjects.text: Ribbon enough to open everything twice. The mill itself is opened daily.

grandProjects.name: The National Umbrella
grandProjects.text: It keeps the whole capital dry. Crispin Mizzle calls it a good start.

grandProjects.name: The Tallest Bandstand
grandProjects.text: No bandstand has ever stood higher. The band is still climbing.

grandProjects.name: Ministry of Ministries
grandProjects.text: It oversees every ministry. A new ministry now oversees it.

twists.name: Bandstand Summer
twists.text: The band plays in every district this term. Brass carries further.

twists.name: Committee Week
twists.text: More committees come to the desk. They have formed one about it.

twists.name: Quiet Press
twists.text: The presses are slow. It takes more gossip to reach the front page.

twists.name: Ribbon Shortage
twists.text: Ribbon is scarce this term. Each cutting costs more, and pleases more.

twists.name: Kite Weather
twists.text: A steady breeze all term. Kites, and the Kite Flyers' League, are up.

twists.name: Market Fortnight
twists.text: Fees bring in more this term. The fortnight lasts all term, as usual.

twists.name: Early Doors
twists.text: Visitors come sooner this term. Some are waiting before the door is open.

twists.name: Hedge Inspection
twists.text: The Tidy Hedge Committee counts for more. It has measured how much.

twists.name: A Gentle Week
twists.text: Saying nothing after a scandal is gentler. Rodney calls it resting.

twists.name: Grievance Amnesty
twists.text: Settling a boycott costs less. Cuthbert has a form for saying sorry.

captions.text: Mayor of Dithering-on-the-Dawdle, unopposed. The other candidate went to the wrong hall.
Governor of Upper Wobbling. A mahogany desk, a green lamp, and Pruella, near lunch.
President. A walnut desk, three telephones, and Mildred, who liked one of the last three.
You serve on, as Acting. Rodney has had that word painted very small on the door.
Every district held. Rodney is having the result framed, and then the frame.
A Quiet Term. Nothing new this time. The clock has been told, and took it well.

places.name: Waitwell
places.note: suggested for the Bus-strong county (county_a): where the province waits for the bus, and waits well

places.name: Gleamford
places.note: suggested for the Shops-strong county (county_b): its shop windows gleam

places.name: Cloche End
places.note: suggested for the Vegetables-strong county (county_c); a cloche is a glass cover for seedlings

places.name: Dawdlemouth
places.note: suggested for the Anglers-strong county (county_e): where the River Dawdle reaches the canal

places.name: Clatterby
places.note: suggested for the Bus-and-Brass county (county_f): buses and bands both clatter

places.name: Hampering
places.note: suggested for the Shops-and-Vegetables county (county_g): a hamper is a basket; hampering is what committees do (a sister to Dithering)

places.name: Wobbling Stone
places.note: written 'the Wobbling Stone': the rocking stone the province is named after; serves no club

places.name: Ribbon Steps
places.note: written 'the Ribbon Steps': the steps of the provincial hall, where every ribbon of the province is cut and every apology made; serves no club (an earlier 'Empty Plinth' was cut: with a numbered bandstand it recalled a real square's famous plinth)

places.name: Second Bandstand
places.note: written 'the Second Bandstand': nobody can find the first; Brass (comedy editor: was 'Fourth Bandstand', which echoes a real square's Fourth Plinth)

places.name: Tiptoe Jetty
places.note: written 'Tiptoe Jetty': the quietest jetty on the canal; Anglers

places.name: Unhurried Canal
places.note: written 'the Unhurried Canal': the province's canal (office-style.md 1)

places.name: Lingering Locks
places.note: written 'the Lingering Locks': a flight of locks on the Unhurried Canal; boats wait in them, anglers watch

places.name: Patient Glasshouse
places.note: written 'the Patient Glasshouse': the oldest of the glasshouses, in no hurry, like the canal; Vegetables (comedy editor: was 'Great Glasshouse', the name of a real botanic-garden building)

places.name: First Shelter
places.note: written 'the First Shelter': the province's oldest bus shelter, kept as it was and leaned on; Bus

places.name: Glass Arcade
places.note: written 'the Glass Arcade': a covered row of shop windows; Shops
